section_summary.extract_value: This section reports reliability and validity analyses for the CEMS (Caregiver Eating Messages Scale) and presents structural equation modeling results examining relationships among caregiver eating messages, body acceptance, body appreciation, and intuitive eating. The study includes a main sample of 238 participants (160 women, 78 men) and a test-retest subsample of 18 young adult students (56% women, 44% men, M age = 20.65, 94% Caucasian). Multiple-group analysis revealed that the path from restrictive/critical eating messages to body appreciation was significantly stronger for men than women, while other structural paths were similar across genders.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents Study 1 results examining the relationships among caregiver eating messages, body acceptance, body appreciation, and intuitive eating for women and men. Table 1 displays means, standard deviations, and correlations for all measured variables, with data from women (n=160) presented below the diagonal and data from men (n=78) presented above the diagonal. The study found that restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages were positively related to BMI and negatively related to body appreciation and intuitive eating, with notable gender differences in several relationships.
